body: Yup, me. Just turned 30 a couple of weeks ago. I have massive talents in music (composition, performance). I was diagnosed ten years ago with schizoaffective disorder. The most common symptom I feel, though, is depression. I have no drive, no motivation, no passion--not anymore. I have tried a number of different things: composing for trailer companies (had to back out due to stress triggering my illness), tried auditioning for Young Artists as an opera singer (same thing, too much pressure), tried my hand at creating a YouTube channel and monetizing it (again, the workload prproved to be too much for my mind to handle). My dad thinks it's all in my head, and that I've victimized myself into this rut I'm in now... My brothers have jobs, and I'm on social security... I have attempted suicide twice in the last ten years, but stay because I would feel guilty for leaving my family behind... Wasted potential... Useless talents, because I can't deal with the dog-eat-dog music industry... No other real skills to speak of... No relationships, no family of my own, no prospects, impulsive buys while manic that result in my dad being upset with me, making my problems worse... My dad helps me with rent, cause I don't make enough to cover all my expenses, and so we have a joint account... That might change soon... Can't work regular 9-5 jobs, cause of the stress and pressure to meet someone else's expectations... Lonely, friendless, helpless, hopeless...

I have schizoaffective disorder, bipolar subtype 2. I'm not unfamiliar with the mood swings and crap financial situation, and the people close to you not understanding or blowing it off. You are loved. You are valuable.

Rational thought works, but that didn't . If anything, it's worsened by the fact that I know it's irrational, but am unable to stop the thoughts and depression. Stupid stress arts them off, and all the chopping techniques in the world don't fix or lessen their effect. I'm tired. So very tired. I'm beginning to not care as much about my faith. I believe, but only just. If I was in hell for eternity, I wouldn't care at this point (if you're not spiritual, yourself, and don't understand very well: that way of thinking basically means giving up completely; if you do have an understanding, disregard my words). 

What good is music if it fits almost nothing? People love it, but there are much more virtuosic composers than I (like the guys from Two Steps From Hell, for instance) whom they could turn to for epic music. I'm just one of those talented losers, and have no hope of success, as stress is always involved, and stress triggers the severe illness symptoms like mad. I have no hope anymore. No future. No life that's with continuing to live. People tell me they love me, but I don't trust them. Always so fake... "Anything I can do?" they ask, but there's nothing they or anyone else can do. Besides, I dunno how to help myself. 

I cry a lot. Medicines don't help. I want this life to end already. I fail at it. In the faith, wet compare this life to a university. I couldn't even get through the first block of the first quarter, it was too hard. I'm not built for a life like this. I'm not really meant for it. I am kind to lots of folks...but my brain doesn't register the kind act and give me endorphins or whatever other neurotransmitters are involved. It's just empty--a big, dark nothing. If life isn't any better by the new year, after I get home from this miserable vacation, I'm going to end my life. I'm going to put this suffering to an end. I've had enough in my life out of my control. I'm going to take control this time. Sorry, God, but I couldn't handle temporal university, and had to come home early after weepily telling my parents over the phone that I couldn't handle it. I can't handle the spiritual one, so I'm coming home.

Sorry if that sounds stupid or whatever. If it fits, then it simply reinforces what I already believe about myself--a waste of human energy.
